# CV model comparison

*Generated by `modeling/src/cv_report.py` on 2026-11-19; do not edit by hand.* Data: `handoff/v1`, train+val pooled (907 rows), StratifiedKFold(5) x seeds [0, 1, 2] = 15 folds. The test split is never loaded. The imputer, scaler, vocabulary, missing-indicator choice, model and (where used) class-bias offsets are all fitted inside each fold's training part; offsets use a nested inner CV.

Feature sets: `A_clinical` 24 non-survey features + missing indicators; `B_clinical_onehot_survey` A + 43 survey items one-hot; `C_clinical_survey_scores` A + survey scores + years_education + marital_status; `D_clinical_engineered` A + ratios. Class order: 0 healthy, 1 pre_diabetes_lifestyle_controlled, 2 oral_medication_and_or_non_insulin_injectable_medication_controlled, 3 insulin_dependent.
Model names: `logreg_C*` balanced multinomial logistic regression; `logreg_grouped_C*_s*` survey columns scaled by multiplier s; `ordinal_logit` / `hgb_monotone` / `hgb_ordinal_free` cumulative (Frank & Hall) models; `+bias` = nested class-offset adjustment. All logistic/ordinal models use 4-class balanced weights.

## 3. Pairwise class separability (clinical features only)

For each pair of classes, only the rows of those two classes are used; a balanced logistic regression (C=1, set `A_clinical`) is cross-validated the same way (5-fold x 3 seeds, stratified on the pair). n = rows of the first / second class. AUC and accuracy at threshold 0.5, mean ± std over folds.

| pair | n | AUC | accuracy | balanced acc. |

| healthy vs pre-diabetes | 332 / 202 | 0.647 ± 0.059 | 0.618 ± 0.050 | 0.610 ± 0.048 |
| healthy vs oral-med | 332 / 282 | 0.866 ± 0.032 | 0.798 ± 0.032 | 0.796 ± 0.033 |

## 4. Staged analysis (explanation of where errors come from, not a competing model)

Stage 1 separates no-medication {healthy, pre-diabetes} from medicated {oral, insulin}; stage 2 splits each side. Same clinical features and logistic regression as above, same folds. Stage-2 rows use the TRUE side (oracle routing) so they show how separable each pair is on its own; the cascade rows below route by the stage-1 prediction.

| step | AUC | accuracy | recall of 1st class | recall of 2nd class |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| stage 1: no-medication {healthy, pre} vs medicated {oral, insulin} | 0.867 ± 0.027 | 0.790 ± 0.029 | 0.798 ± 0.033 | 0.778 ± 0.058 |
| stage 2a (true side): healthy vs pre-diabetes | 0.647 ± 0.059 | 0.618 ± 0.050 | 0.642 ± 0.073 | 0.577 ± 0.074 |
| stage 2b (true side): oral-med vs insulin | 0.674 ± 0.076 | 0.684 ± 0.050 | 0.729 ± 0.037 | 0.541 ± 0.129 |

Stage-2 numbers differ slightly from section 3 because the folds are drawn from the full data here, not from the pair's own rows.

Where the errors of the final 4-class decision fall (all 15 test folds pooled):

|  | flat 4-class logreg (share of errors) | hard cascade (share of errors) |
|---|---|---|
| wrong side (no-med ↔ medicated) | 43.5% | 42.4% |
| healthy ↔ pre-diabetes | 33.8% | 34.3% |
| oral-med ↔ insulin | 22.7% | 23.3% |
| all errors (count over 15 folds) | 1371 | 1348 |
| accuracy | 0.496 ± 0.051 | 0.505 ± 0.044 |
| macro-F1 | 0.464 ± 0.053 | 0.475 ± 0.045 |

43% of the flat model's errors put the row on the wrong side of the no-medication / medicated line (this includes pre-diabetes ↔ oral-med confusions); routing through stage 1 first does not change the error mix materially.

## 5. Limits

- **Neighbouring classes overlap.** The classes are ordered by treatment intensity, not by separable physiology; section 3: the three lowest-AUC pairs are exactly the three adjacent ones (healthy vs pre-diabetes 0.65, pre-diabetes vs oral-med 0.79, oral-med vs insulin 0.68). For the reference model accuracy is 0.50 but adjacent-class accuracy is 0.88, so 75% of its errors are exactly one class off.
- **Few insulin rows.** train+val has 91 insulin-dependent rows (class counts: healthy 332, pre-diabetes 202, oral-med 282, insulin 91); in a 5-fold test part that is about 18 per fold, so insulin recall moves in steps of roughly 5 percentage points per row.
- **A 160-row validation set is noisy.** The official validation split has 160 rows (healthy 40, pre-diabetes 40, oral-med 47, insulin 33). A recall near 0.34 on 40 pre-diabetes rows has a 95% interval of about ±0.15 from sampling alone, and the fold-to-fold std of reference macro-F1 on ~181-row folds is 0.053. Differences of a few hundredths of macro-F1 measured on validation alone are not evidence.
- **Selection optimism.** Every grid point above is reported and none was chosen on these numbers here; picking the best row by this same CV would be optimistically biased. One design choice was made after seeing CV output: the ordinal models first balanced each binary problem separately, which gave incoherent probabilities, and were changed to shared 4-class balanced weights.
- Nothing in this report uses test rows or labels.
